questions.html: In a KNN classifier with K = 5, if the majority class among the 5 nearest neighbors is class A, what is the predicted class for a new data point?
questions.solution:
(a)
In KNN classification, the predicted class for a new data point is determined by the majority class among its A nearest neighbors.
Since the majority class among the 5 nearest neighbors is class A, the predicted class for the new data point is class A.

questions.html: In a logistic regression model, if the odds ratio for a predictor variable is 2.5, what is the estimated increase in the odds of the outcome for a one-unit increase in the predictor variable?
questions.solution:
2.5
The odds ratio represents the change in odds of the outcome associated with a one-unit increase in the predictor variable. In this case, an odds ratio of 2.5 implies that the odds of the outcome increase by a factor of 2.5 for every one-unit increase in the predictor variable.

questions.html: In a naive Bayes classifier, if the probability of class A given the predictor variables is 0.7 and the probability of class B given the same predictor variables is 0.3, what is the predicted class for a new data point?
questions.solution:
(a)
In a naive Bayes classifier, the predicted class for a new data point is the class with the highest posterior probability given the predictor variables. In this case, since the probability of class A is higher (0.7 > 0.3), the predicted class for the new data point is class A.

questions.tags: Technical • Data Science and artificial Intelligence • +2 / -0.66
questions.html: In a Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) model with two classes, if the Mahalanobis distance between a new data point and the mean of class A is 3 and the Mahalanobis distance between the same data point and the mean of class B is 2, what is the predicted class?
questions.solution:
(b)
In LDA, the predicted class for a new data point is the class with the smallest Mahalanobis distance.In this case, the Mahalanobis distance is smaller for class B (2 < 3), so the predicted class for the new data point is class B.

questions.html: In a logistic regression model, if the odds ratio for a predictor variable is 0.4, what is the estimated decrease in the odds of the outcome for a one-unit increase in the predictor variable?
questions.solution:
(b)
The odds ratio represents the change in odds of the outcome associated with a one-unit increase in the predictor variable. In this case, an odds ratio of 0.4 implies that the odds of the outcome decrease by a factor of 0.4 for every one-unit increase in the predictor variable. Therefore, the estimated decrease in the odds is 1 – 0.4 = 0.6.

questions.html: In a supervised learning dataset, if there are 100 labeled examples and each example has 10 features, how many labels are there in total?
questions.solution:
(b)
In supervised learning, each example in the dataset is associated with a label. Since there are 100 labeled examples in the dataset, there are a total of 100 labels.

questions.html: In an unsupervised learning dataset with 500 examples and 15 features each, what is the total number of labels?
questions.solution:
